thread:
Maya: Heads up - p95 on /embeddings jumped in the dashboard after yesterday's routing policy tweak. p50 is stable, p99 nudged up. Anyone else seeing this?
Jon: Yep. I see a jump for requests with client-affinity=mobile. Weirdly it's only in the 'merged routes' view, not the raw endpoint breakdown.
Maya: Confirmed. In endpoint-breakdown (no merge) mobile p95 looks normal. In merged view blended p95 climbs ~80ms. Could be a weighting/merge issue.
Sasha: Sounds like quota annotations interacting with merge. We add route_quota tags when fallback/burst kicks in. If merge logic loses provenance or misweights quota_buckets, percentiles can skew.
Kevin: Quick repro: ran side-by-side queries for include_merge=false vs true. Counts identical but p95 diverges. Paste: 
Kevin: ```
include_merge=false: p50 35ms p95 220ms p99 610ms  count=12.4k
include_merge=true:  p50 36ms p95 300ms p99 650ms  count=12.4k
```
Jon: Count parity implies samples aren't dropped; distribution blending changes the quantiles.
Sasha: Hypothesis: we merge using tdigest rollups per route weighted by route_count. If high-latency samples are concentrated in a small quota_bucket that ends up with lower merge weight, those tails get muted in some merges and amplified in others depending on order.
Maya: Could client-affinity label assignment vs actual route used cause some mobile traffic to appear under a different origin in merged view? We added affinity routing last week.
Kevin: Also the console applies smoothing_window=60s post-merge; that can exaggerate a transient cluster when route weights shift.
Maya: Action items: Kevin - run deterministic replay for a 1h window capturing raw samples and merged tdigest outputs; Sasha - audit merge weighting and provenance preservation; Jon - add a notice in the dashboard rollout UX explaining merged-percentile caveats. If merge weighting is wrong we gate the rollout.
Jon: I'll add a rollout dialog note: "Merging by route may change observed percentiles; see provenance badge for sample origin".
Sasha: Can metrics-bot add a provenance mini-badge in the latency tooltip listing top origin tags (route, quota_bucket, affinity) for the current slice? That will help folks triage without guessing.
metrics-bot: Ack — I'll add a tooltip badge with up to 3 top origin tags and a link to the raw-sample query. ETA 48h.
Maya: If this is a merge-weighting bug, consider switching default merge_mode->conservative for canaries until fixed.
Kevin: I'll attach the repro query + raw sample dump once done.
Maya: Thanks all.
Maya: quick note — if anyone wants to debug together tomorrow, ping me in #eng-platform-debug. :thumbsup:
